records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:214 — A client-wide grant is ignored whenever that client already has any per-client resource, so adding an unrelated specific permission can unexpectedly revoke global admin API access to that client.
records.rationale: Looking at ClientPermissionsV2.java lines 207-224, the hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope) method first checks for a per-client resource: `resource = resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())`. If found (not null), it evaluates permissions on that resource. If not found (null), it falls back to checking the 'all-clients' resource type permission. records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:78 — An all-clients view grant returns true before evaluating an explicit client-specific denial, exposing clients that the policy excludes.
records.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a potential authorization bypass in ClientPermissionsV2.canView(ClientModel client) at line 79. The method first checks `canView()` which returns true if the user has global VIEW permission (line 85: `return canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)`). If this returns true, the method short-circuits and returns true without checking client-specific permissions.
